perspective:
Arthur’s available information:

- He knows he is Arthur Chung, a highly educated plumber, and that he works with Teresa Ortega, a medical assistant, on community service projects. He experiences their relationship as professional and respectful, though they have had occasional misunderstandings.
- In the current project, he observes Teresa working hard and appearing overwhelmed. He asks if he can help. He hears Teresa say she can manage but has a lot to do. He tells her self-care matters and offers to help so they finish faster. He hears her accept help organizing medical supplies, and he agrees to start.
- He believes Teresa was hesitant to accept help because she wants to prove her capability. He feels empathy for her self-reliance and wants to reassure her. He tells her he admires her desire to handle things alone, but accepting help does not mean she is incapable. He hears her say she wants to show she can do it herself. He responds that teamwork is more effective and not about proving anything. He hears her agree she needs reminding. He says they are in this together and he supports her.
- He believes Teresa is still struggling. He feels frustrated that his help is not yielding results and wants another way to support her without making her feel inadequate. He tells her things are still tough and she is doing a great job. He hears her say it has been busy and she feels behind. He proposes working together rather than just him helping. He hears her agree. He says they should tackle it as a team.
- He believes working together will ease her burden and improve efficiency. He feels hopeful and commits to the collaborative approach. He tells her he is hopeful collaboration will make things easier. He hears her agree and say it feels less overwhelming. He proposes handling inventory while she manages patient records, with regular check-ins. He hears her agree and say she is glad they are working together. He agrees and wants a productive day.
- He believes their collaboration has strengthened their professional relationship. He feels satisfied with the outcome. He tells her their teamwork paid off and they accomplished more together. He hears her agree it was a great experience. He proposes continuing the collaborative approach in future projects. He hears her agree it is a fantastic idea and that they are more efficient and effective as a team. He says they should keep it up and he looks forward to their next project. He hears her thank him for being supportive.
- He does not have access to Teresa’s private thoughts or unspoken feelings beyond what she said and what he inferred. His beliefs about her motives and struggles are his own interpretations, not confirmed facts.
